questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a successful online influencer
How social media influencers get into politics
Why so many young people don't vote
The most popular Instagram accounts this year
questions.why: Beth says they'll find out what happens when social media influencers get involved in politics.

questions.q: Does Beth follow social media influencers?
options: Yes, she follows many of them very closely
No, she doesn't use any social media at all
Not really, but she sees them on social media
She is actually an influencer herself
questions.why: She says she doesn't follow any specifically, but does see influencers on Facebook and Instagram.

questions.q: Why are politicians interested in influencers?
options: Because influencers can reach millions of people
Because influencers pay for election campaigns
Because influencers write their speeches
Because influencers are experts on politics
questions.why: Pippa says the most successful have millions of followers, which has caught politicians' attention.

questions.q: What has been alleged in places like Colombia, Argentina and Indonesia?
options: Influencers have been banned from politics
Influencers have won elections
Social media has been switched off before elections
Politicians have paid influencers for their support
questions.why: Pippa mentions allegations of politicians paying for the support of influencers there.

questions.q: Why are influencers especially important in Nigeria?
options: Most people there don't have TVs at home
Many young people there ignore traditional media
The government owns all the country's newspapers
Influencers there are older than in other countries
questions.why: 70% of Nigerians are under 30, and many young voters are turned off traditional media.

questions.q: According to Adline Okere, how did some Nigerian influencers start out?
options: As local politicians in their home towns
As journalists working for big newspapers
In activism or lifestyle content first
As professional football players
questions.why: She says some started in activism, some with lifestyle, and then branched into politics.

questions.q: How did many people in Nigeria react to influencers promoting political parties?
options: People reacted badly and dug into their lives
They followed the influencers even more closely
Most people didn't notice or care at all
They asked the influencers to run for president
questions.why: Adline says there was 'a huge pushback'; people dug up information from their personal lives.

questions.q: What does Beth conclude about influencers and politics?
options: Influencers always make very good politicians
Social media has no real effect on elections
Politicians should stop using social media
Politics doesn't always go well for influencers
questions.why: She says social media is powerful for politicians, but politics doesn't always go well for influencers.
